newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q1 current account gap widened to $40.97 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q1 current account gap widened to $40.97 bln.

text.p: The U.S. current account, seasonally adjusted, as reported by the Commerce Department.
Net data--Govt. transfers, U.S. assets abroad and foreign-held assets.
Wall Street economists had forecast a $44.5 billion deficit for the first quarter.

The department said that it had revised its methods for collecting data and calculating current account, which resulted in changes to its previous estimates for much of the data from 1974 to 1996. It said the new data permitted improvements to be made particularly for more recent years' estimates.

Among the changes cited were improved estimates of income receipts from U.S. holdings of foreign stocks and bonds as well as revisions to previous estimates of royalties and license fees, income payments and capital flows.

As a result of the revisions, the department's previous estimate of the 1996 current account deficit was revised down sharply to a $148.18 billion shortfall from a previously reported deficit of $165.10 billion.
The revised 1996 current account deficit of $148.18 billion was the largest for any year since 1987 when it was a revised $168.05 billion.
The revisions reduced the previous estimates of current account deficits in every year from 1988 through 1996.
